{
  "question_intent": "Bank earnings-call questions on structural hedge, deposit stability, and regulatory outlook",
  "main_topics": ["structural hedge", "deposit stability", "regulatory outlook"],
  "answer_completeness": "Partial",
  "response_stance": "Direct",
  "evidence_level": "High",
  "contains_numeric_evidence": true,
  "contains_forward_guidance": false,
  "narrative_alignment": "Aligned",
  "question_quote": "Can I ask you again about the reinvestment of the maturity over the next three years, whether or not you are taking a slightly more upbeat view of that, in terms of that stability of whether perhaps this flags risk to the £2 billion kind of income target there?",
  "answer_quote": "So, we're obviously been observing the macro trends, both in terms of deposits and swap rates. But what we try to do in February is set out clear targets, our clear objectives, what's important to us, to allow them to be tracked. Our actual experience is that, swap rates will move around. They moved around significantly. So what we are not going to do is mark to market those targets on a quarterly basis.",
  "reason": "The answer addresses the reinvestment of maturity and the bank's approach to setting targets, but does not fully answer the question about the £2 billion income target risk or the regulatory outlook."
}
